hunks.baseline: His sculpted, handsome features were part of it, but more than that, they were overwhelmed by the intense presence radiating from him.
hunks.sol: His sculpted features were striking enough, but it was the intense presence radiating from him that overwhelmed them.

hunks.baseline: “Wake up from your dream.”
hunks.sol: “Stop dreaming.”

hunks.baseline: “Who said anything? It’s just because I’ve never seen his face before.”
hunks.sol: “Who said I was? I’ve just never seen him before.”

hunks.baseline: “Didn’t you see him earlier? When the Third Young Master’s pavilion collapsed?”
hunks.sol: “Didn’t you see him earlier, when the Third Young Master’s pavilion collapsed?”

hunks.baseline: “With all that chaos, do you think I only saw one or two people? Still, I don’t think I’d ever forget that man, even if I’d seen him in the middle of a war. Hehe.”
hunks.sol: “With all that chaos, who could keep track of every face? Still, I don’t think I could forget that man even if I saw him in the middle of a war. Hehe.”

hunks.baseline: “True enough. His appearance was a complete disaster back then.”
hunks.sol: “True. He was in quite a state back then.”

hunks.baseline: The maid thought about it for a moment, then her eyes went round.
hunks.sol: The maid thought for a moment, then her eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, no way?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, don’t tell me…”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. He’s the Second Young Master. So stop dreaming nonsense and go do your work.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. He’s the Second Young Master. So stop dreaming and get back to work.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung ignored the whispers around him with an indifferent expression and continued walking.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung ignored the whispers around him and continued on with an indifferent expression.

hunks.baseline: When he reached the stately, traditional pavilion, the martial artists guarding the entrance opened the doors for him. The looks of awe came free of charge.
hunks.sol: When he reached the stately, old-fashioned pavilion, the martial artists guarding the entrance opened the doors for him. The looks of awe were a bonus.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung spread his arms wide and pulled Jin Mukyung into a tight embrace.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung threw his arms wide and pulled Jin Mukyung into a tight embrace.

hunks.baseline: For a moment, Mukyung considered dodging, but if he did, he would have to watch that hulking body whine like a child.
hunks.sol: For a moment, Mukyung considered dodging. But if he did, he would have to watch that hulking man whine like a child.

hunks.baseline: “Even if we had not seen each other for thirty years, my answer would be the same.”
hunks.sol: “I would say the same if it had been thirty.”

hunks.baseline: A short while later, the two brothers sat across from each other and began to talk.
hunks.sol: A short while later, the two brothers sat across from each other.

hunks.baseline: “Sir Wipeng is nowhere to be seen.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t see Sir Wipeng.”

hunks.baseline: Wipeng, who was supposed to remain at the Lesser Family Head’s side like a shadow, was absent.
hunks.sol: Wipeng, who should have been at the Lesser Family Head’s side like a shadow, was nowhere to be seen.

hunks.baseline: After taking a sip of tea, Jin Wikyung answered.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung took a sip of tea before answering.

hunks.baseline: If Taiyuan, where the family was located, was the center of Shanxi, Three Questions Gorge was practically at its entrance and far edge. It was also a crossroads leading to Shaanxi and Henan, so even fifteen days was a tight schedule.
hunks.sol: If Taiyuan, where the family was based, lay at the heart of Shanxi, Three Questions Gorge was practically its gateway and outermost edge. It was also a crossroads leading to Shaanxi and Henan, so even fifteen days would be a tight schedule.

hunks.baseline: “It’s only a formality anyway. Aren’t you making him work too hard?”
hunks.sol: “It’s only a formality. Aren’t you putting him through too much?”

hunks.baseline: “Why? Feeling sorry for him?”
hunks.sol: “Why? Feel sorry for him?”

hunks.baseline: “I didn’t expect things to get this big.”
hunks.sol: “I didn’t expect things to get this out of hand.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s not—”
hunks.sol: “That wasn’t—”

hunks.baseline: Unlike before, Jin Wikyung’s eyes held a light reproach. Jin Mukyung sighed.
hunks.sol: Unlike before, Jin Wikyung’s gaze held a mild reproach. Jin Mukyung sighed.

hunks.baseline: “I didn’t intend to take it that far. At first, I only meant to exchange a few moves.”
hunks.sol: “I didn’t mean to take it that far. At first, I only intended to exchange a few moves with him.”

hunks.baseline: He had personally exchanged blows with Jin Taekyung only an hour or two earlier. By now, he could no longer refuse to acknowledge the truth.
hunks.sol: He had traded blows with Jin Taekyung himself only a shichen or two earlier.[^1] He could no longer deny it.

hunks.baseline: “Since we’re on the subject, what on earth happened?”
hunks.sol: “Since we’re on the subject, what exactly happened?”

hunks.baseline: “The youngest?”
hunks.sol: “With the youngest?”

hunks.baseline: “Everything. The letter I received only said that the Mount Heng Sword Sect bastards were invading.”
hunks.sol: “With everything. The letter I received only said that those Mount Heng Sword Sect bastards were invading.”

hunks.baseline: A carrier hawk had been sent immediately after the Mount Heng Sword Sect declared war, so there had been no way for him to learn the details.
hunks.sol: A messenger eagle had been dispatched immediately after the Mount Heng Sword Sect declared war, so there had been no way for him to learn the details.

hunks.baseline: The rumors he had heard on the way to the Jin Family of Taiyuan were all he knew.
hunks.sol: All he knew were the rumors he had heard on his way to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

hunks.baseline: “It goes all the way back to the Great Faction War forty years ago.”
hunks.sol: “It goes back forty years, to the Great Faction War.”

hunks.baseline: “Back then, the Head Elder… Wait, what did you say?”
hunks.sol: “Back then, the Head Elder… What did you say?”

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung emptied his teacup in one gulp, and Jin Wikyung’s face filled with disbelief.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung tossed back the rest of his tea, and Jin Wikyung stared at him in disbelief.

hunks.baseline: It was, after all, the hidden history of the family. Jin Mukyung had always been a man who cared about nothing but martial arts, but Jin Wikyung had never imagined he could be this bad.
hunks.sol: This was the family’s hidden history, after all. Jin Mukyung had always cared about nothing but martial arts, but Jin Wikyung had never imagined he could be this bad.

hunks.baseline: “You need to know! The direct line of our family—”
hunks.sol: “You need to know! You’re a direct descendant of our family—”

hunks.baseline: “The Head Elder betrayed us. Then he died. The Mount Heng Sword Sect was destroyed in the process. The Jin Family of Taiyuan was the final victor. Did I misunderstand anything?”
hunks.sol: “The Head Elder betrayed us. Then he died. The Mount Heng Sword Sect was destroyed in the process. The Jin Family of Taiyuan emerged victorious. Have I misunderstood anything?”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung began to wonder which of them was the abnormal one.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung was beginning to wonder which of them was the strange one.

hunks.baseline: Then he suddenly remembered something.
hunks.sol: Then something suddenly occurred to him.

hunks.baseline: “You were the one who said you wanted to hear everything!”
hunks.sol: “You were the one who asked me to tell you everything!”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, I take that back. If I listen to things that happened before I was even born, I’ll grow old and die right here. I’d rather spend that time swinging my sword one more time.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, I take that back. If I have to hear about things that happened before I was even born, I’ll grow old and die right here. I’d rather spend that time swinging my sword one more time.”

hunks.baseline: “Training? Right now?”
hunks.sol: “T-Train? Now?”

hunks.baseline: “I came to spar with Sir Wipeng after so long, but he’s gone. Shouldn’t I train by myself, at least?”
hunks.sol: “I came hoping to spar with Sir Wipeng after all this time, but he isn’t here. I may as well train alone.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung answered the heartfelt call coldly.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung answered the heartfelt cry coldly.

hunks.baseline: “The tea was good. Thank you.”
hunks.sol: “Thank you for the tea.”

hunks.baseline: He left the office without even looking back.
hunks.sol: He left the office without looking back.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung stared at the back of his departing younger brother, stunned.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung stared after his departing younger brother in shock.

hunks.baseline: Both his second and youngest brothers had grown up so much. He was proud of how wonderfully they had each matured, but sometimes, moments like this still hurt.
hunks.sol: Both his second and youngest brothers had grown up so fast. He was proud of the fine men they had become, but sometimes, moments like this still left him feeling hurt.

hunks.baseline: *Yes. This is the natural order of things.*
hunks.sol: *Yes. I suppose this is the natural order of things.*

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung let out a sigh that seemed to drain the earth itself, then sat down in front of his worktable.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung let out a sigh deep enough to sink the earth, then sat at his worktable.

hunks.baseline: He carefully began piecing together the unfortunate masterpiece that had been torn apart earlier: *The Birth of a Hero*.
hunks.sol: He carefully began piecing together the ill-fated masterpiece that had been torn apart earlier: *The Birth of a Hero*.

hunks.baseline: At his subordinate’s report, Wipeng swallowed a bitter smile.
hunks.sol: At his subordinate’s report, Wipeng swallowed a bitter laugh.

hunks.baseline: There had never been an assassin in the first place. Naturally, there would be no traces to find.
hunks.sol: There had never been an assassin in the first place. Naturally, there were no traces to find.

hunks.baseline: *I have to put on an act I was never meant to perform.*
hunks.sol: *I can’t believe I have to play a part I was never born for.*

hunks.baseline: A conversation he had shared with Jin Wikyung an hour earlier flashed through Wipeng’s mind.
hunks.sol: The conversation he had shared with Jin Wikyung a shichen earlier flashed through his mind.

hunks.sol: That was when the smile vanished from his lord’s face.

hunks.sol: *An opportunity for our family to bring all of Shanxi Province together under its banner.*

hunks.sol: *I’ll assign thirty elites to you. Head south immediately. Your official objective is to capture or kill the assassin, but your true mission is something else.*

hunks.baseline: *On the coming New Year’s Day, I intend to summon every sect in Shanxi Province to our family.*
hunks.sol: *On the coming New Year’s Day, I intend to summon every sect in Shanxi Province to our family estate.*

hunks.baseline: *Are you trying to become the Alliance Leader?*
hunks.sol: *Do you intend to become the Alliance Leader?*

hunks.baseline: Until recently, Shanxi Murim had appeared to the outside world as two towering peaks: the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
hunks.sol: Until recently, Shanxi Murim had appeared to the outside world to be divided between two towering peaks: the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect.

hunks.baseline: But the reality was different. Shanxi Murim was shaped like a three-legged cauldron.
hunks.sol: But the reality was different. Shanxi Murim was more like a three-legged cauldron.

hunks.sol: The Jin Family of Taiyuan held the central region, while the Mount Heng Sword Sect held the north. The south belonged to more than twenty small and mid-sized sects.

hunks.baseline: The Five Gates of Shanxi, which had vanished in the recent war, was merely the name given to the five especially powerful sects among them.
hunks.sol: The Five Gates of Shanxi, which had vanished in the recent war, was merely the collective name for the five most powerful among them.

hunks.baseline: *Their alliance is strong. They may refuse to comply.*
hunks.sol: *Their alliance is strong. They may refuse to answer the summons.*

hunks.baseline: *They might have, if this had been before the war.*
hunks.sol: *They might have, before the war.*

hunks.baseline: And the Jin Family of Taiyuan had both the strength and the justification to support Shanxi Murim’s cauldron alone.
hunks.sol: And the Jin Family of Taiyuan now possessed both the strength and the justification to stand as the sole support of the cauldron that was Shanxi Murim.

hunks.sol: There had only ever been one answer.
